topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional Modalities and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address traditional cancer treatment approaches—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated toxicities and efflux-mediated drug resistance.

topics.label: Targeting Intrinsic Cellular Vulnerabilities and Checkpoint Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies designed to exploit specific cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint failures, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeting Oncogenic Kinases and Mechanisms of Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale, design, and clinical use of small molecule kinase inhibitors targeting oncogenic driver mutations, as well as the diverse resistance mechanisms that emerge.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the application of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies to target surface antigens directly and to deliver cytotoxic payloads selectively to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer Immunosurveillance and Immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and clinical strategies for re-engaging the immune system, including checkpoint blockade, bispecific engagers, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Current Challenges, Paradigms, and Future Directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the systemic challenges, epidemiological trends, and future paradigms in cancer care, concluding with the clinical dilemma of testing novel therapies against established cytotoxic regimens.
